prompt: A wave pulse travels along a rope at 5 m/s. What is true of an individual piece of the rope?
answer: It oscillates about a fixed position while the pattern moves on
options: It travels along the rope at 5 m/s with the pulse, since the pattern is made of moving rope pieces
It moves ahead of the pulse and then falls behind
It oscillates about a fixed position while the pattern moves on
It moves forward when the pulse is a crest and back when a trough
explanation: Wave speed is how fast the pattern propagates. Each piece of rope only oscillates locally (transversely), and its speed changes continually, unlike the constant propagation speed.
hint: Picture a stadium wave: do the spectators travel round the stadium?

prompt: Two small waves overlap and the resulting displacement is exactly the sum of the two. What property of the medium allows this?
answer: The wave equation is linear in the displacement
options: The waves are travelling in the same direction
The medium is perfectly rigid
The wave equation is linear in the displacement
The waves have the same amplitude
explanation: If the wave equation is linear, sums of solutions are solutions. Large amplitudes in a real medium can make the response nonlinear, and superposition then fails.
hint: What mathematical property lets solutions be added?

prompt: A pipe closed at one end and a string fixed at both ends are both driven at their fundamental. Why do their overtone sequences differ?
answer: Different boundary conditions select different allowed wavelengths
options: Strings support odd harmonics and pipes support even harmonics
Pipes have a smaller fundamental than strings
Sound travels faster than waves on a string
Different boundary conditions select different allowed wavelengths
explanation: Modes are standing waves that fit the boundaries. Fixed–fixed fits whole half-wavelengths (all harmonics); closed–open fits odd quarter-wavelengths (odd harmonics only).
hint: Count the nodes and antinodes each set of ends demands.

prompt: Wavelength in metres for speed 340 m/s and frequency 170 Hz?
A sound wave travels at 330 m/s with frequency 110 Hz. Find wavelength in metres.
An ideal pipe is closed at one end and open at the other. Which harmonics does the simple model allow?
answer: Only odd multiples of the fundamental
options: Only even multiples of the fundamental
Only the fundamental, with no overtones
Only odd multiples of the fundamental
All integer multiples, as for a fixed string
explanation: A displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end fit an odd number of quarter-wavelengths, so L = (2n−1)λ/4 and only odd harmonics appear.
hint: Sketch the node at one end and the antinode at the other, then count quarter-wavelengths.

prompt: A wave has frequency 5 Hz and wavelength 2 m. Find phase speed in m/s.
A sound wave crosses a room at 343 m/s. Which statement about the air molecules is correct?
answer: Each molecule shuffles back and forth around its place
options: Each molecule shuffles back and forth around its place
Just the molecules at the source take part in it
Each molecule travels across the room at 343 m/s
Molecules in the crests move forward, those in troughs backward, at 343 m/s
hint: Separate the pattern speed from the motion of the material.
explanation: The phase velocity describes how the compression pattern moves. Individual molecules oscillate with small displacement, and their thermal motion is a separate random motion.
